name: altorank
description: Agent-readiness audits, Search Console reporting, keyword research and SEO drafts into a human review queue. Every publish is attributed to a named person, by a click or by a rule they set; the MCP server has no approve or publish tool.

interface.longDescription:
AltoRank writes search and AI-search content for websites you own or manage.

From a chat you can check whether an AI assistant can read a site (nine checks covering AI-crawler rules, sitemaps, structured data and machine-readable content), propose the JSON-LD a page is missing, read Google Search Console performance, find keyword cannibalisation and coverage gaps, get keyword suggestions, move the content calendar, and generate SEO drafts.

Drafts land in a review queue inside AltoRank. Every publish is attributed to a named person: an approval in the editor, or an automatic-publishing rule they set that emails each draft and ships it after a hold window (24 hours by default) unless they hold it. No tool approves, deletes or publishes a draft, and no endpoint behind one does; the one publish-side tool retries a failed publish of an article a person already approved. Assistants prepare work; people decide what goes live.

The readiness tools work on any public domain. The account tools need an AltoRank workspace and a connection you authorise, with write access opt-in on the consent screen and revocable under Settings, API keys.

AltoRank is open source (AGPL-3.0) and can be self-hosted.
interface.defaultPrompt: Check whether an AI assistant can read my site and tell me what is failing.
